title: The Persian Conquest of Yemen and the Conversion of Badhan
overview: This episode details the transition of Yemen from Ethiopian to Persian control following the efforts of Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan to reclaim his ancestral land. It highlights the miraculous events surrounding the Prophet Muhammad's ‷ letter to the Persian Emperor Kisra and the subsequent conversion of the Persian governor Badhan to Islam.
lessons: Wisdom and strategy are often needed to deal with powerful and greedy leaders.
Seeking help from foreign powers can often lead to a 'betrayal' or larger problems than the original issue, as seen in the Uqdah of Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan.
Arrogance (takabbur) and the mistreatment of messengers can lead to the downfall of even the mightiest empires.
True guidance is a gift from Allah; some hearts accept the truth upon seeing a single sign, while others remain closed even after witnessing great miracles.

chapters.title: The Rule of Abrahah's Sons
chapters.summary: Following the destruction of Abrahah's army in the Year of the Elephant, the land of Yemen remained under the control of the Ethiopians (Ahabash). Control passed to Abrahah's son Yaksum, and subsequently to another son, Masruq. The native Yemenis felt like foreigners in their own land, living under the laws and rules of the occupying forces. This period of foreign rule set the stage for a local uprising led by the Yemeni royal family.
key_points: The Ahabash (Ethiopians) continued to rule Yemen after Abrahah's death.
Yaksum ibn Abrahah took charge of Yemen initially.
Masruq ibn Abrahah succeeded his brother Yaksum.
The Yemeni people were subservient to foreign occupiers.

chapters.title: Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan Seeks an Ally
chapters.summary: Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan, a member of the original Yemeni royal family, sought to reclaim Yemen for his people. He first traveled to Syria to ask the Roman Emperor (Qaysar) for military aid, but was refused because the Romans had originally supported the Ethiopian occupation. Sayf then turned to Numan ibn al-Mundhir, the Arab king in Iraq, who also lacked the power to confront the Ahabash. Numan suggested that Sayf accompany him on his annual visit to the Persian Emperor, Kisra, who possessed the most powerful army in the world.
key_points: Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan was from the royal family of Rabiah ibn Nasr and the Tubba.
The Qaysar (Caesar) refused to help because he had initially ordered the Habashi intervention.
Numan ibn al-Mundhir was an Arab king in Iraq of Yemeni origin.
Numan suggested seeking help from Kisra, the leader of the Persian Empire.

chapters.title: In the Court of Kisra
chapters.summary: Sayf visited the palace of Kisra, the 'King of Kings' (Shahanshah), and witnessed the immense opulence of the Persian court. Kisra sat on a jewel-encrusted throne with a 90kg crown suspended from the ceiling by gold ropes so as not to crush him. While other visitors performed full prostration (sujood), Sayf only bowed his head, which angered the Emperor. Sayf explained that his preoccupation with the occupation of his homeland distracted him, prompting Kisra to consult his advisors about helping the Yemenis.
key_points: Kisra was known by the title Shahanshah (Malik al-Muluk).
The Persian crown weighed 90 kilograms and was suspended from the ceiling.
Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan refused to perform full sujood to Kisra.
Kisra's advisors initially discouraged helping because they saw Yemen as a land with no riches (khayrat).

chapters.title: The Ruse of the Mountains of Gold
chapters.summary: To secure Persian help, Sayf employed a clever plan to appeal to Kisra's greed. After receiving 10,000 silver dirhams as a gift, Sayf threw the coins into the streets, claiming they were worthless because Yemen possessed 'mountains of gold and silver.' Intrigued by this potential wealth, Kisra agreed to send an army. Following his advisors' suggestion, he released 800 prisoners from death row to fight, ensuring that he would lose nothing regardless of the battle's outcome.
key_points: Sayf threw away 10,000 dirhams to pique Kisra's interest.
Sayf claimed Yemen had mountains of gold and silver.
Kisra sent 800 prisoners who were on death row.
General Wahriz, a master sharpshooter, was appointed to lead the prisoners.

chapters.title: The Battle for Yemen
chapters.summary: The Persian force, led by General Wahriz and joined by Sayf's Arab supporters, landed at the port of Aden to confront Masruq ibn Abrahah's army. During the battle, Wahriz asked to identify the leader and targeted Masruq once he switched from an elephant to a horse, and finally to a slow mule. Wahriz shot an arrow that hit the red pearl on Masruq's forehead, killing him instantly and ending Ethiopian rule. However, the Persians betrayed Sayf by keeping control of Yemen for themselves, a situation known to Yemenis as the 'Uqdah of Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan.'
key_points: The army landed at the port of Aden in Yemen.
Masruq ibn Abrahah was identified by the red pearl on his forehead.
Wahriz shot Masruq while he was on a mule, symbolizing his humiliation.
The Persians took control of Yemen rather than handing it to Sayf.

chapters.title: The Prediction of Kisra's Death
chapters.summary: Yemen was governed by a series of Persian rulers, the third of whom was Badhan. During his reign, the Prophet Muhammad ‷ sent a letter to Kisra calling him to Islam, which Kisra arrogantly tore up. In response, the Prophet ‷ predicted that Allah would tear up Kisra's kingdom and informed Badhan's messengers that Kisra had been killed that very night. When the news reached Yemen 14 days later confirming the exact date and time of Kisra's death, Badhan recognized this as a sign of true prophethood.
key_points: Badhan was the third Persian ruler of Yemen.
Kisra tore the Prophet's ‷ letter out of arrogance (takabbur).
The Prophet ‷ predicted the destruction of the Persian Empire.
The news of Kisra's death arrived in Yemen 14 days after the Prophet ‷ announced it.

chapters.title: Guidance and the Hearts of Men
chapters.summary: Badhan and the Persians in Yemen embraced Islam after witnessing the Prophet's ‷ miraculous knowledge. The Prophet ‷ allowed Badhan, and later his son Shahr, to remain as the leaders of Yemen. This conversion is contrasted with the Quraysh, who saw the miracle of the moon splitting yet remained stubborn in their disbelief. The episode concludes by emphasizing that guidance is a gift from Allah and previews the upcoming discussion on the lineage of the Prophet ‷.
key_points: Badhan and his Persian subordinates in Yemen became Muslims.
The Prophet ‷ confirmed Shahr ibn Badhan as the ruler after his father's death.
Al-Aswad al-Ansi was a false prophet (Dajjal) who later killed Shahr.
Guidance is compared between the receptive Badhan and the stubborn Quraysh.

The second Persian governor of Yemen.
Throne.

The Arabian Peninsula.
Good things, riches, or natural resources.

A past king of Yemen and ancestor of Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan.

Prostration.

segments.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
And may the peace, blessings, and prayers of Allah be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions.
segments.translit: Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā Nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn.

segments.en: O Allah, teach us what benefits us, benefit us with what You have taught us, and increase us in knowledge.
segments.translit: Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wanfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa zidnā ʿilmā.

segments.text: Last week we left off with the story of how [[Allah|الله]] [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] destroyed [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and his forces when they came from [[Yemen|اليمن]] to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]],

and how [[Allah|الله]] [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] destroyed [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and destroyed his army, and protected His house, the house of [[Allah|الله]] [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
And we mentioned that [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] was the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], but actually he was a Habashi, he was from what is known in modern times as Ethiopia.
And we spoke about how the Ethiopians, how the [[Ahabash|أحباش]] took control of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] was the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]] at that time.

But when he left to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], when he left with his army towards [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with the intention of destroying the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], he left his son [[Yaksum|يكسوم]], [[Yaksum|يكسوم]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] in charge of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
So even after [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and his army that he had taken with him to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], even after they were killed and they were destroyed,
the country of [[Yemen|اليمن]] or the land of [[Yemen|اليمن]], it still remained under the rule of the [[Ahabash|أحباش]].
It still remained under the rule of the Ethiopians, with the son of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], [[Yaksum|يكسوم]], being in command.
And when [[Yaksum|يكسوم]] died, his brother, the brother of [[Yaksum|يكسوم]], his name was [[Masruq|مسروق]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], he took control of the kingdom.
So the family of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], or the son of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], was still ruling the kingdom of [[Yemen|اليمن]].

And at that time, during the time of [[Masruq|مسروق]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], there was a young man, his name was [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Dhi Yazan|ذو يزن]], and he was from the original royal family of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
He was from the family of [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]], who we spoke about before.
And he was from the family of the [[Tubba|تبع]], the original Yemenis who ruled [[Yemen|اليمن]].
So he had royal blood in him, he was from the royal family and he was a pure Yemeni, and his name was [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Dhi Yazan|ذو يزن]].
And of course, you know, him seeing his country and his people occupied by these [[Ahabash|أحباش]], by these Ethiopians, he and his people, the Yemenis,
they don't have any say in what goes on in their own country, and they have to watch these foreigners rule their land and make their laws and make their rules,
and they have to be subservient to them.
So [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Dhi Yazan|ذو يزن]], he was very, very upset with the situation,
and he wished to find a way to get the control of [[Yemen|اليمن]] back to the Yemenis, and preferably himself, because he was from the original royal family of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
So he wanted to think of a way: how can we take the power back from these [[Ahabash|أحباش]], from these Ethiopians who have occupied our land?
So he was able to gather some support from the Arabs, but not nearly enough to overthrow the government of [[Masruq|مسروق]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]].
There was no way that he could face the army of [[Masruq|مسروق]]. And he knew that, he knew that, 'No, this is not even a battle that's worth fighting.
I have some support with the Arabs, but there's no way that we can face [[Masruq|مسروق]] and his army.'
So he thought, 'Okay, who else can I ask for help? Who is more powerful than the army of the [[Ahabash|أحباش]]?
I need to find a leader or a ruler who is stronger than these [[Ahabash|أحباش]].
And if I can get them to help me, then we can take over this land once again.'
So he took a trip to [[Sham|شام]]. He went over to [[Sham|شام]], the Greater Syria area, where he met with the [[Qaysar|قيصر]]. And the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] was in [[Sham|شام]].
And he asked the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] for help. He said, 'You know, these [[Ahabash|أحباش]], they took over the land of my forefathers, and they occupied our land, and they're still ruling our land.
I want to get what is rightfully mine, I want to get the land of [[Yemen|اليمن]] back to control of the Yemenis.'
But the [[Qaysar|قيصر]], he didn't want to hear any of it.
Because if you remember, the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] was actually the one who sent a letter to the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] in [[Habashah|حباشة]] to go over to [[Yemen|اليمن]] and fight the Yemenis.
This was actually from an order from the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] himself.
Because we talked about what happened in [[Yemen|اليمن]], and how [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], who was the son of the [[Tubba|تبع]] and he was a Yemeni,
how he killed the Christians in [[Yemen|اليمن]] by digging trenches and throwing them into those trenches of fire.

And when the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] heard of this, and the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] was a Christian, the [[Qaysar|قيصر]], he sent a letter to the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] of [[Habashah|حباشة]] to send an army to [[Yemen|اليمن]] to get revenge on [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]].
And that's what they did.
And that is how the Habashis took control of [[Yemen|اليمن]] in the first place, by this order from the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] to the [[Najashi|نجاشي]].

So now, when [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Dhi Yazan|ذو يزن]], he goes back to the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] and asks for help to get our, to get his land back, then of course the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] is not going to help him.

Because the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] is the one who sent the [[Ahabash|أحباش]] to [[Yemen|اليمن]] in the first place by ordering the [[Najashi|نجاشي]], or by requesting the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] to send his army to [[Yemen|اليمن]].
So the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] didn't want to hear anything from [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Dhi Yazan|ذو يزن]]. And he didn't help him at all, and he didn't give him anything.
So now [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] is upset, and he's thinking, 'You know, what can I do? I need to do something to get the land of my forefathers back.'
So he thought at that time, 'Look, the [[Qaysar|قيصر]], he didn't help me. The best bet I have is to seek help from someone who is from the Arabs.
I'm not going to seek help from the non-Arabs, I will go to an Arab and seek help from him.'
So he went to Iraq. He went to Iraq and the king there at that time, he was a man named [[Numan ibn al-Mundhir|نعمان بن المنذر]].
[[Numan ibn al-Mundhir|نعمان بن المنذر]], and he was the king, and he was a big king there in Iraq, and he was originally Yemeni as well.
He was originally Yemeni, but he was settled there in Iraq and he became a king there in Iraq.

So when [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Dhi Yazan|ذو يزن]] went to [[Numan ibn al-Mundhir|نعمان بن المنذر]] in Iraq and asked him for help to get the land of [[Yemen|اليمن]] back under Yemeni control,
[[Numan ibn al-Mundhir|نعمان بن المنذر]], he understood the plight of [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]]. And he said, 'You know, I understand your situation, and I'm not unwilling to help you.
I would help you if I could help you, but you know that army of the [[Ahabash|أحباش]], that Habashi army, it's a really strong and it's a really big army.'
'And you know, my army and my people, it's not strong enough to confront that army.
I know my limit, I know my power, I know the power of my army, and there's no way that we would be able to defeat that army.
But I have a suggestion for you.'
'If you just stay with me for a little while, every year I take a trip to visit the [[Kisra|كسرى]].
The [[Kisra|كسرى]], that's the leader of Persia, the leader of the Persian Empire.' He said, 'Every year, I and a group of my people, we take a trip to visit the [[Kisra|كسرى]].
If you want to stay until that time with me, you can stay, and then we will go together to the [[Kisra|كسرى]] and you can ask him for help.'
'And the [[Kisra|كسرى]], he was the most powerful man in the world, and his army was the most powerful army in the world. That was the superpower of that time.'
So this is what [[Numan ibn al-Mundhir|نعمان بن المنذر]] suggested to [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Dhi Yazan|ذو يزن]]: 'Just stay with me here.
When the time comes for us to go and visit the [[Kisra|كسرى]], which we do every year, you come along with me, you meet him, you talk to him, you explain to him your situation.'
'Maybe he will offer to help you, and if he helps you, that army can easily destroy the army of the [[Ahabash|أحباش]].'
So [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Dhi Yazan|ذو يزن]], he thinks that this is a good idea. This is a smart plan.
'So let me stay here in Iraq, and when [[Numan ibn al-Mundhir|نعمان]] is going to visit the [[Kisra|كسرى]], I will go with him and I will explain my situation to the [[Kisra|كسرى]] himself.'

So when that time came for [[Numan ibn al-Mundhir|نعمان بن المنذر]] to go and visit the [[Kisra|كسرى]], [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] [[ibn|بن]] [[Dhi Yazan|ذو يزن]] accompanied him, and they went to the palace of the [[Kisra|كسرى]].
Now like we said, the [[Kisra|كسرى]] was the most powerful man in the world at that time, and his kingdom was the biggest and most powerful kingdom of that era.
So he was very, very well respected and feared, even by other kings. Other kings didn't consider him...
to be their counterpart or their equal. Other kings considered him to be their king,
and that's why he was also known with the title [[Shahanshah|شاهنشاه]], which means in Persian, which translates to [[Malik al-Muluk|ملوك الملوك]], or the king of kings.
So even the other kings, they considered him their king. So they didn't consider him to be an equal counterpart, rather they respected him more.
So they went to his palace. Now, the way that he would present himself
is that anyone who came into his [[majlis|مجلس]], anyone who came into his gathering, they would come into his gathering, and he would be behind a curtain.
So the people are all here in the room, and they would not be sitting down, they would be standing.
They would not sit in front of the [[Kisra|كسرى]] because this would be considered in their...
in their belief, a sign of disrespect. So they would all be standing. And the [[Kisra|كسرى]] would be behind a curtain,
and he would be on a throne, and that throne was surrounded with jewels. There were jewels all over that throne.
And he had a huge crown. The [[Kisra|كسرى]], he had such a huge crown,
and it is said that that crown weighed 90 kilograms. The crown weighed 90 kilograms.
Now you're thinking, how can anyone put a 90 kilogram crown on their head without being crushed? And this is a good question.
The way that he used to do it is that this 90 kg crown, it would actually be suspended with gold ropes onto the ceiling of the palace.
So there were these gold ropes coming down from the ceiling of the palace, and on the bottom of those ropes, the 90 kg crown was suspended.
In such a position over his throne, that he would position himself and sit there, and the crown would be right on his head, without putting any pressure on his head.
So he had this huge crown suspended from the ceiling, and he had this huge [[arsh|عرش]], this big throne with jewels all around it, and he was behind this curtain.
So the people, they would come, and they would wait for that curtain to be opened.
So when they came, [[Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir|النعمان بن المنذر]] came, and [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]] had accompanied him as well.
So they were there standing with all of the other people to see the [[Kisra|كسرى]]. So the [[Kisra|كسرى]] sat on his throne,
he had the crown suspended from the ceiling on his head, and the curtain was opened.
And when that curtain was opened, everyone, all of those kings and whoever had come to visit the [[Kisra|كسرى]], they would go down in [[sujood|سجود]] to the [[Kisra|كسرى]].
They would all go down into [[sujood|سجود]] to the [[Kisra|كسرى]], [[wa al-iyadhu billah|والعياذ بالله]]. So when [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]] was here among this gathering,
all of them made [[sujood|سجود]] to the [[Kisra|كسرى]] except [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]]. He didn't make [[sujood|سجود]]. Rather, he just bent his head.
He just bent his head lightly, but he did not go down into [[sujood|سجود]].
So when the [[Kisra|كسرى]] saw this, he saw and he was expecting everyone to make [[sujood|سجود]] to him, but he saw that this one man didn't make [[sujood|سجود]] to him.
So he became very, very angry, and he said:

segments.translit: man hādhā al-aḥmaq alladhī lam yasjud lī

segments.text: Who is this fool who didn't make prostration to me?
So they brought him to the presence of the [[Kisra|كسرى]], and he was asked, why didn't you make [[sujood|سجود]] to him when everyone else did?
And then [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] said, "It's just the worries that I have in my mind, you know, I was preoccupied thinking about my situation,
and that's what distracted me from making [[sujood|سجود]] to you when everybody else made [[sujood|سجود]]."
So then the [[Kisra|كسرى]] asked, "What are these worries? What are these concerns that are preoccupying you, [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]]?"
And then he saw that as the opportunity to tell his story,
that his ancestors were the kings of [[Yemen|اليمن]], the rulers of [[Yemen|اليمن]], and then these [[Ahabash|أحباش]], these Ethiopians, they came and occupied their land,
and they occupy our land to this day. And I'm just thinking of a way to get my land back for my people.
And I am from royal blood as well.
So the [[Kisra|كسرى]] listens to [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] tell his story. So he consults his advisors about this situation.
He asked them, "What do you think? Should we help this guy out? Should we help him get his land back from the [[Ahabash|أحباش]]?"
And the advisors say, "Look, you can do it easily. I mean, our army is so much stronger than their army, but what is the benefit for us in doing that?
Why do we need to put ourselves on the line to help out this guy?
And the land of the Arabs, it is a land with no [[khayrat|خيرات]].
There's no good in that land, it's not an agricultural land, it's not a land with any type of riches or anything.
Why do we need to go and put ourselves on the line, get some of our soldiers killed in order to help out this guy? This is none of our business."
So the advisors advised [[Kisra|كسرى]], don't help him out. Let him do whatever he wants, leave him, but you know, we don't need to help him.
So the [[Kisra|كسرى]] told [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] his decision that, no, we're not going to help you out, but just so
he wouldn't leave empty-handed, because the [[Kisra|كسرى]] felt that if he sent [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] away with nothing,
then [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] would talk about the [[Kisra|كسرى]], "You know, I went and I visited him, and I came back with nothing," and that would be bad on the reputation of the [[Kisra|كسرى]].
They had this reputation that they wanted to uphold as people of generosity. You know, someone comes to you, and you will never let them leave empty-handed.
So this was the attitude of the [[Kisra|كسرى]] as well. So he knew that he couldn't let him go empty-handed with nothing, because he didn't want his own reputation to be harmed.
So he said, "I'm not going to help you by sending an army with you or anything, but here, take 10,000 silver dirhams."
Take 10,000 silver dirhams, and he gave him 10,000 silver dirhams.
Now, this is a huge amount of money. 10,000 silver dirhams was a huge, huge amount of money.
But this is not what [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]] came for. He didn't come for money. He came to get help in reclaiming the land of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
So he thought of a plan. Once he had this money with him, he had these 10,000 silver dirhams, he thought of a plan to still get the help of the [[Kisra|كسرى]].
So he left the palace with those 10,000 dirhams, and then he started just throwing them out in the street like that.
And the people, they saw, and they started jumping and gathering around and trying to catch whatever they could. Imagine a guy going out in the street, throwing out $100 bills.
You can imagine what type of a scene it would be. So that's the type of scene it was.
[[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] is throwing out these silver dirhams and people are jumping and trying to catch and get whatever they can.
So when this news came back to the [[Kisra|كسرى]], that this is what this guy is doing with the gift that you gave him, he's throwing it out in the streets and people are collecting it,
then the [[Kisra|كسرى]] thought to himself, "There is something about this young man. There is something about him. Bring him back. Bring him back."
So they brought him back to the presence of the [[Kisra|كسرى]], and the [[Kisra|كسرى]] asked him, "This is what you do with the gift that I gave you?
You throw it in the streets like that?"
And then [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] implemented the plan that he had thought of. His plan was to
bring out the greed in the [[Kisra|كسرى]]. He knew that these are greedy people. So his plan was to bring out that sense of greed and use that sense of greed
to get him to send his army to help him out. So what did he say?
He said, "Yeah, the reason why I'm throwing around these silver coins is because this is of no use to me.
"You know, in my country in [[Yemen|اليمن]], we have mountains of gold and silver. We have mountains that are made of gold and mountains that are made of silver.
So what are these coins to me? It's nothing."
So then the [[Kisra|كسرى]] said, "What? You have mountains of gold and silver in [[Yemen|اليمن]]? That's not something that I ever heard before."
So his greed is coming up now.
Like, wow, if we actually go to that land and help him out, and we take control of that land, we will have mountains of gold and silver.
So he goes to his advisors again. The [[Kisra|كسرى]] goes to his council again and asks them for advice.
He says, "I found out from this guy, from [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]], that there are mountains of gold and silver in [[Yemen|اليمن]], so maybe we should actually go and help him out."
So the advisors say, "Look, we have a good idea for you. This is how you should handle this. Don't send our army.
"Don't send our army, because we don't want any casualties in our army. But what we should do is,
"we have so many prisoners. We have so many prisoners who are on death row that are waiting to be executed.
"Let us just send them with [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]], and let them fight. And if they win, that's great! Then you have control of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
"And if they lose, then they die anyways, and it saves you from the trouble of having to execute them. So either way you win.
"So let's just release these prisoners who are on death row, and let them be the army that accompanies [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]] to take control back of [[Yemen|اليمن]]."
So the [[Kisra|كسرى]] thought, "This is a great idea. I have nothing to lose here. Either I win and I get the land,
"or I lose, and those prisoners who I was going to execute anyways, they get executed for free."
So he thought this is a fool-proof plan. This is perfect. So he releases those prisoners who were on death row, and it is said that...
there were 800 of them, and they were big criminals.
So 800 of these criminals are now going to accompany [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]]...
...from the [[Persian|فارس]] Empire back to [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And he also sent a very good general of his to lead that army.
Now this is, you know, this army of 800 people, they don't have any military experience or anything. They don't know how to fight, so they need a commander.
They need a leader who can guide them in the battle.
So he actually did send one of his good generals to be the leader of these prisoners, of these criminals.
And the name of this general was [[Wahriz|وهرز]].
And [[Wahriz|وهرز]] was a very, very smart and a very, very good soldier.
And he had such good aim when he would shoot an arrow, he was able to hit his target perfectly, and he was known for this.
So they sent 800 of these criminals under the command of the general [[Wahriz|وهرز]], and he also sent eight ships, eight boats to go from [[Persia|فارس]] to [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]], now he's very happy. He said, "Now I have my big army here, you know.
They're going to help me out and we're going to get control of our land once again."

So they leave and they go through the Euphrates River, and then they go through the Persian Gulf, and then they go through the Arabian Sea, and finally they land at the port of Aden in [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And they come off.
And [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]], he had his own people there, the [[Arabs|عرب]], that he was able to gather from before.
You know, they were not very big in number, but he had some support.
So he gathered them as well, and they all joined together: the [[Arabs|عرب]] that [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] had originally gathered plus these new people from [[Persia|فارس]], these criminals,
and they formed their army under the command of the general [[Wahriz|وهرز]].
And the [[Ahabash|أحباش]], they had already gotten wind of this as well. They knew, they knew that this army is coming to fight them.
They had gotten the news of it, and they were ready, they were prepared.
So as soon as they landed, as soon as the [[Persian|فارس]] army landed with [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]], the fighting started, and the [[Ahabash|أحباش]] were ready for this fighting.
Now the leader of the [[Ahabash|حبشي]] army was [[Masruq|مسروق]] himself.
He took command of the army himself.
He didn't appoint a general to take control, rather he was in control of his own army, and he was in the battlefield himself, [[Masruq|مسروق بن أبرهة]].
So [[Wahriz|وهرز]], the fighting is going on, and [[Wahriz|وهرز]], who is the general, the commander of the [[Persians|فرس]]...
...he said, "Show me who is the leader of this army. Who knows who is the leader of the [[Ahabash|حبشي]] army?"
So [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]], of course he knows who it is. He said, "It is [[Masruq|مسروق]], I know him. He is that one over there.
Do you see the man on the elephant?"
He was on an elephant.
"Do you see the man on an elephant who has a red pearl on his forehead between his eyes?"
[[Masruq|مسروق]] used to wear some jewelry, and from that jewelry was a red pearl that he would have on his forehead, and it was between his eyes.
He said, "That is [[Masruq|مسروق]], he is the leader, the guy on that elephant with the red pearl in between his eyes."
So [[Wahriz|وهرز]] said, "Okay, that's him. Let me know when he gets off of the elephant."
"Let me know when he gets off of that elephant."
So after some time, he gets off of the elephant and he gets on a horse instead.
So they tell [[Wahriz|وهرز]], they said, "He got off the elephant and now he's on the horse."
So then [[Wahriz|وهرز]] said, "Okay, he's on the horse. Let me know when he gets off the horse."
So after some time, he gets off the horse and now he is on a mule.
Now he is sitting on a mule.
So they tell [[Wahriz|وهرز]], "Yes, now he's sitting on the mule."
So he said, "Okay, now he's sitting on a mule, okay. He is humiliated and his kingdom will now be humiliated as well."
And as you know, a mule, it's a slow animal. It's a very slow animal.
So the reason why [[Wahriz|وهرز]] didn't want to get him while he was on the elephant or the horse was because, like we said, he was a sharpshooter.
He knew how to shoot that bow and that arrow.
So if he's on a fast-moving target, it would be very difficult to hit it.
But if he's on something slow like a mule, that will be the perfect opportunity to hit him.
So when [[Wahriz|وهرز]] saw that [[Masruq|مسروق بن أبرهة]] is on a mule now, he said, "Okay, this is our chance."
So he gets an arrow and he aims. And he's in the back of the army here, he's not in the front even, he's behind the army.
And [[Masruq|مسروق]] is pretty far away. And of course [[Masruq|مسروق]] has his people around him as well, trying to defend him.
But this guy [[Wahriz|وهرز]] was such a sharpshooter and he had such a perfect aim...
...that he shot his arrow and hit him right in that red pearl that he had on his forehead.
So the arrow hit him right in the forehead, right on that pearl, and it came out through the back of his head.
So [[Masruq|مسروق]] falls down, [[Masruq|مسروق]] is dead.
The commander of the [[Ahabash|حبشي]] army, the leader of [[Yemen|اليمن]], is dead.
And the [[Persians|فرس]] have won.
So the army that [[Kisra|كسرى]] sent has won this battle.
So now [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]], he's very happy. This is what he wanted.
But now, they stabbed [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]] in the back as well. They said, "We're not giving it to you, we're going to keep this for ourselves."
So instead of giving it to [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]] as he hoped that they would do—this is why he asked them for their help in the first place—now the [[Persians|فرس]],
they said, "Now we're going to be in control of this land. We're not going to give it back to you Yemenis."
So [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف]], he felt like he was stabbed in the back.
And up to this day, any type of agreement that the Yemenis make with some outside forces that leads to bigger problems than they had before, they call it...
..."[[uqdah|عقدة]] [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]]". "This is an [[uqdah|عقدة]] [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]]". This is like the agreement of [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سيف بن ذي يزن]].
When the Yemenis, when they try to get help from the outside, it ends up that the problems they have after that are bigger than the problems that they originally had in the first place.
So this is exactly what happened. And now the [[Persians|فرس]] have control of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
So the [[Kisra|كسرى]], he appointed a ruler to rule [[Yemen|اليمن]], and the name of this ruler was [[al-Murzuban|المرزبان]].
So [[al-Murzuban|المرزبان]] was the one that the [[Kisra|كسرى]] appointed to rule [[Yemen|اليمن]]. And after he died, then it went to [[al-Tabyujan|التبجان]].
So it went from [[al-Murzuban|المرزبان]] to [[al-Tabyujan|التبجان]].
And then the [[Kisra|كسرى]], he had some problems with [[al-Tabyujan|التبجان]], so he removed him from that position, and he replaced him with a man named [[Badhan|باذان]].
So the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]] appointed by the [[Kisra|كسرى]] was a man named [[Badhan|باذان]]. First [[al-Murzuban|المرزبان]], then [[al-Tabyujan|التبجان]], and the third one was [[Badhan|باذان]].
Now it was during the time that [[Badhan|باذان]] was the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]] that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]]'s message came.
And the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], as we know, he sent letters to many of the different rulers, right?
You know that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] sent letters to the different rulers of different kingdoms, and one of the letters that he sent was to the [[Kisra|كسرى]].
One of the letters that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] sent was to the [[Kisra|كسرى]] in [[Persia|فارس]].
And when the [[Kisra|كسرى]] received this letter from the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], he was very angry, and he ripped it up and threw it without even reading it.
He ripped it up and threw it without even reading it, and he killed the messenger...
...that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] sent with that letter.
Imagine that! The way that they used to communicate with each other is that they would send messengers.
The Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] would have a letter, and he would send a messenger to go and deliver it to the recipient.
And it was commonly known from everybody that you don't kill the messenger.
You don't kill the messenger. This was considered immoral and unethical in all of the kingdoms. Yet still, the [[Kisra|كسرى]], out of his arrogance, out of his [[takabbur|تكبر]]...
...he ripped up the letter of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] before even reading it, and he killed the messenger as well.
And when the news of this reached back to the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], he said...

segments.translit:
Laqad mazzaqa risālātī, mazzaq Allāhu mulkah.. Laqad mazzaqa risālātī, mazzaq Allāhu mulkah.. = He ripped up my letter, may Allah rip up his kingdom.. He ripped up my letter, may Allah rip up his kingdom.. = لقد مزق رسالتي، مزق الله ملكه.. لقد مزق رسالتي، مزق الله ملكه.. 

 speech: 
 text: He ripped up my letter, may Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] rip up his kingdom.

 speech: 
 text: So the [[Kisra|كسرى]], he killed the messenger of the Messenger [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], and he sent his own messenger to [[Badhan|باذان]].

 speech: 
 text: And we said [[Badhan|باذان]] was the one that he appointed to rule [[Yemen|اليمن]]. So the [[Kisra|كسرى]] sent a messenger of his own to [[Badhan|باذان]]...

 speech: 
 text: ...because he knew that [[Yemen|اليمن]] is near where the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] is.

 speech: 
 text: So the [[Kisra|كسرى]] sent his messenger to [[Badhan|باذان]] and gave him the message that, "There is this man in the [[Jazirat al-Arab|جزيرة العرب]]..."

 speech: 
 text: "...and he wrote me such and such letter. I want you to send some people to him to bring him to me. Bring him to me."

 speech: 
 text: So [[Badhan|باذان]], to obey the command of his ruler, to obey the command of the [[Kisra|كسرى]], he sent two men.

segments.text: And those two men came to the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] and said,
just surrender yourself to us.
Come with us to the [[Kisra|كسرى]], surrender yourself to us, and we will not bring our army to fight you.
So then the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] said, "Oh, were you sent by the [[Kisra|كسرى]]?" And they said, "Yes."
And then he said,

segments.translit: Inna Allāha qad qatala Kisrā al-laylah Usul al-Din.

segments.text: Surely Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] has killed the [[Kisra|كسرى]] tonight.
So they said to him, "Okay, even if what you're saying is true,
if he has died, our [[Kisra|كسرى]], if he died tonight like you're saying, how do you know?
It takes one month for news to come from Persia to here.
And you're saying this happened tonight? He was killed tonight, and you're telling me right now? How do you know?"
And then he said, "From [[wahy|وحي]], I get revelation from Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]]. Your [[Kisra|كسرى]] is dead, and he died tonight."
So these two men were surprised,
and they go back to [[Badhan|باذان]] in [[Yemen|اليمن]].
They go back to [[Yemen|اليمن]], and they go back to [[Badhan|باذان]], and they said,
We went to him, and this is what he said. He said that the [[Kisra|كسرى]] was killed tonight.
So then [[Badhan|باذان]] says, "We haven't received any news about this.
What day did he say that?" And then they told him the exact day that he mentioned it.
So [[Badhan|باذان]] said, "Okay, let us wait. Let us wait and see if any news comes to us about this."
So 14 days later,
14 days later, the message comes from Persia that the [[Kisra|كسرى]] has died.
And when they look into the date when exactly his death occurred, it was the exact date that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] mentioned it.
So [[Badhan|باذان]] says, "There is no way that this could have been known by anyone except a Prophet."
"So this man, he must be a Prophet of Allah. I believe in him."
And he became a Muslim. [[Badhan|باذان]] became a Muslim, and those Persians that were there in [[Yemen|اليمن]] with him, they all became Muslims as well.
So this is how Islam came into [[Yemen|اليمن]]
through the hands of [[Badhan|باذان]],
who was the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. Now [[Badhan|باذان]],
he retained the kingdomship of [[Yemen|اليمن]], and the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] allowed that.
The Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was in agreement of that.
And then after [[Badhan|باذان]] died, the kingdomship of [[Yemen|اليمن]] went to the son of [[Badhan|باذان]],
his name was [[Shahr|شهر]].
And the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] also agreed to this.
He didn't try to change the leadership of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. He allowed it to stay with [[Badhan|باذان]] while he was alive, and he allowed it to go to [[Shahr|شهر]] after [[Badhan|باذان]] had died.
Then towards the end of the life of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]],
there was a man in [[Yemen|اليمن]], his name was [[al-Aswad al-Ansi|الأسود العنسي]].
And he was a liar. He was one of the minor [[Dajjals|دجالين]] who claimed to be a Prophet,
and he actually killed [[Shahr|شهر]] ibn [[Badhan|باذان]].
And that was towards the end of the life of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]].
So this is actually how
Islam came into [[Yemen|اليمن]]
on the hands of a Persian who was appointed to rule [[Yemen|اليمن]] by the name of [[Badhan|باذان]].
And it shows how Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] guides whom He wills through His signs.
The [[kuffar|كفار]] of the [[Quraysh|قريش]], they were shown signs as well, but they didn't believe.
They asked the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] to split the moon into two pieces.
And the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] said to them, "If I show you this sign that you're asking for, will you believe?"
They said, "Yes, we will believe." So the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] asked Allah to show them this sign, and Allah split the moon into two pieces,
and it was seen by the [[Quraysh|قريش]] with their own eyes. Yet still they didn't believe. They said, "This is magic."
They said, "This is magic."
So guidance is from Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
Even if a person sees all the signs, if Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] has put a seal on that person's heart, they will never be guided.
[[Badhan|باذان]] on the other hand, Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] opened his heart to Islam.
He saw this sign, that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] knew the exact day that the [[Kisra|كسرى]] died,
and there's no way that he could have known this except through revelation from Allah. So he accepted that and he became a Muslim.
Guidance is from Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], and we ask Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] to keep us upon guidance.
Don't worry, we're not skipping over anything.
You may be thinking that how are we already talking about the time when the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] is writing letters to the kings. No, we're not skipping anything.
We have to go back and forth sometimes, [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], just to get a good picture of exactly how things are going.

Next week, [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], we will talk about, we'll go back to [[Makkah|مكة]], [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], and we will go back to the lineage of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] and we'll talk about

who was the first person who began the tribe of [[Quraysh|قريش]], where did the [[Quraysh|قريش]] come from, and we will talk about the ancestors of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] and his lineage, [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]].
We'll get into that next week, [[bi-idhnillah|بإذن الله]]. [[Wallahu a'lam|والله أعلم]].
[[Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammad wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn|وصلى الله وسلم وبارك على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين]].

review.q: Who ruled Yemen after the death of [[Abrahah|أفبْرهه]]?
review.a: Control passed first to his son [[Yaksum|فكسوم]], and subsequently to another son, [[Masruq|مسروق]]. The native Yemenis lived as subordinates under the laws of the [[Ahabash|أباش]].

review.q: Why did [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سف بن ذو فزن]] seek help from [[Kisra|كسرى]]?
review.a: He wanted to reclaim Yemen for his people from the [[Ahabash|أباش]] occupation. After the [[Qaysar|فصر]] refused to help, he was advised by the king of Iraq to seek an alliance with the Persians.

review.q: What were the notable features of the [[arsh|عرش]] and crown of [[Kisra|كسرى]]?
review.a: The throne was jewel-encrusted and the crown weighed 90 kilograms. The crown was suspended from the ceiling by gold ropes so that it would not crush the Emperor.

review.q: Why did [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سف بن ذو فزن]] claim that Yemen had 'mountains of gold'?
review.a: This was a clever ruse to appeal to the greed of [[Kisra|كسرى]] and convince him to send an army. To prove the claim, Sayf threw away 10,000 silver dirhams as if they were worthless.

review.q: How did General [[Wahriz|وهرز]] end Ethiopian rule in Yemen?
review.a: He identified [[Masruq|مسروق]] by the red pearl on his forehead and shot an arrow that hit it, killing him instantly. This victory at the port of Aden led to the collapse of the [[Ahabash|أباش]] occupation.

review.q: What lesson does the '[[uqdah|عقاء]] of [[Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan|سف بن ذو فزن]]' teach?
review.a: It shows that seeking help from foreign powers can lead to a betrayal where the ally becomes the new occupier. The Persians kept control of Yemen for themselves instead of handing it to Sayf.

review.q: What miraculous news did the Prophet ﷺ share with [[Badhan|باذان]]'s messengers?
review.a: He informed them that Allah had killed [[Kisra|كسرى]] that very night. When news confirming the exact date and time reached Yemen 14 days later, [[Badhan|باذان]] accepted Islam.

review.q: What lesson does the speaker draw regarding the heart and guidance?
review.a: Guidance is a gift from Allah; some, like [[Badhan|باذان]], accept the truth after one sign, while others remain stubborn despite great miracles. This contrast is seen in the differing reactions of the Persians and the Quraysh.
